incoming.name: Indonesia
incoming.excerpt: European traders first arrived in the early sixteenth century seeking to monopolize the sources of nutmeg, cloves, and cubeb pepper in The Moluccas.

outgoing.name: Black pepper
outgoing.excerpt: Commercial cubebs consist of the dried berries, similar in appearance to black pepper, but with stalks attached — the "tails" in "tailed pepper".

outgoing.name: England
outgoing.excerpt: The modern employment of cubeb in England as a drug dates from 1815.

outgoing.name: Europe
outgoing.excerpt: In 14th century, cubeb was imported into Europe from the Grain Coast, under the name of pepper, by merchants of Rouen and Lippe.

outgoing.name: India
outgoing.excerpt: Cubeb came to Europe via India through the trade with the Arabs.

outgoing.name: Poland
outgoing.excerpt: Ocet Kubebowy, the vinegar infused with cubeb, cumin and garlic was used for meat marinades in Poland during the 14th century.

outgoing.name: Sanskrit
outgoing.excerpt: In China this pepper was called both vilenga, and vidanga, the cognate Sanskrit word.

outgoing.name: Sumatra
outgoing.excerpt: It is mostly grown in Java and Sumatra, hence sometimes called Java pepper.
